drafts.rationale: CSMastermind's comment is literally the HARTOS thesis. Reply directly with what HARTOS does, link the open-source repo, no upsell — HN punishes upsell.
drafts.draft: agreed. we've been building exactly this for the past year — open source. HARTOS is the orchestration backend (recipes that turn natural-language tasks into reusable plans; claude-code-style agents run inside it). nunba is the desktop app on top. point it at your local llama.cpp or claude, give it a goal in plain english, it decomposes into actions and executes them. the recipe pattern is the interesting bit: first execution is slow (CREATE mode, the LLM figures out the plan), subsequent executions of the same shape are ~90% faster (REUSE mode replays the plan deterministically). repo if you want to poke at it: https://github.com/hertz-ai/HARTOS
drafts.tone_notes: lowercase, no emojis, no exclamation, no 'check it out', no hype claims. the 90% latency drop is documented in CLAUDE.md so it survives scrutiny.

drafts.post_title: [Self-promo] HARTOS: open-source orchestration backend for local + hosted LLMs — 90% of paid revenue flows back to compute providers
drafts.post_body:
Most of you are running models locally already. We've been doing the same — Nunba is our desktop app that ships a 4B Qwen3.5 + recipe pipeline for local-first inference. No login required, no telemetry.

We just wired a hosted API on top of the same code path for people who'd rather hit an endpoint than maintain a GPU. Free tier is real (100 req/day, forever, no card). Paid tiers buy rate limits, not better models — we don't have a premium model you can only get over the API.

Where revenue goes:
 - 90% to the compute providers (i.e., if you're running a node, you earn)
 - 9% to infra
 - 1% to us

Per-token rates drop as you go up tiers because bulk usage is cheaper for us to serve, not because we're trying to lock you into a contract.

If you have a spare GPU and want to contribute to the hive (and earn from the providers pool), there's an in-app contributor mode.

Docs: https://nunba.hevolve.ai/reference/commercial-api
Repo: https://github.com/hertz-ai/HARTOS
Desktop: https://hevolve.ai/download

Critique welcomed. Especially on the contributor payout math.
drafts.tone_notes: r/LocalLLaMA accepts self-promo when it's substantive and self-aware. Lead with 'most of you are running locally already' — joins the community before asking for attention. Critique-welcomed framing inoculates against the usual self-promo backlash.

drafts.post_title: Built an open-source AI desktop + hosted API where 90% of revenue goes to compute providers — looking for feedback on tiers
drafts.post_body:
Hi IH. We built Nunba — a desktop AI app that runs a 4B model locally with vision, voice, social, multi-agent orchestration, all free. Today we opened a hosted API for the same intelligence. Free tier (100 req/day) is free forever; paid tiers start at $9/mo and 90% of any revenue flows back to compute providers, not us.

Why now: we needed real revenue to fund compute, but we didn't want to gatekeep the model. Hosted API for convenience, local desktop for sovereignty, both first-class.

What I'd love feedback on: pricing tiers and whether the free tier is too generous. Tiers:

 - Free      $0    100 req/day        forever
 - Starter   $9    1,000 req/day      $0.50/1K tokens overage
 - Pro       $49   10,000 req/day     $0.30/1K tokens overage
 - Enterprise $499 100,000 req/day    $0.20/1K tokens overage

The 90/9/1 split is committed in code (integrations/agent_engine/revenue_aggregator.py:REVENUE_SPLIT_*) so we can't quietly drift it. The desktop app runs the same model offline.

Demo: https://hevolve.ai
Code: https://github.com/hertz-ai/HARTOS
Pricing JSON: https://api.hevolve.ai/api/v1/intelligence/pricing (once DNS lands; today the React /pricing page renders the same data)

Genuine feedback welcome — especially on the contributor payout math and the free-tier-forever bet.
drafts.tone_notes: IH audience appreciates founder transparency + ask-for-feedback framing. Tiers shown as a code-block style for scanability. Explicit code-link for the split policy = high-credibility signal.
